reason: Start with the kidney's filter by joining the capillary tufts to their surrounding capsules.
expectation: I expect a filtering unit that lets some blood contents enter the capsule, though the details may need further parts.

alternatives.reason: The transport proteins also seem important for reclaiming useful substances, but filtration is a natural starting point.

effect: The filter also lets useful substances through, so the next priority is a selective recovery route.
reaction: The distinction between filtration and recovery is useful.
reason: Add transport proteins to the tubule walls to prepare for reclaiming useful substances.
expectation: I expect tubules equipped to move glucose, salts and water selectively, although they may still need a blood supply.

effect: The tubules now have selective transport proteins; they can be connected to the filter and blood supply.
reaction: The separate positions of the pump and glucose carrier are a useful detail.
reason: Connect filtration to recovery so the filtered fluid has a route into the tubules.
expectation: I expect a connected filtering and recovery unit, though it may still need blood-vessel branches.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the blood vessels also seems necessary, but I want to join the filter to the tubules first.

effect: The filter and recovery tubule now form a nephron; connecting blood vessels is the next step toward returning reclaimed substances to circulation.
reaction: The labelled nephron makes the assembled unit easier to recognize.
reason: Connect the working units to the kidney's blood-vessel branches.
expectation: I expect vessels to supply the filters and run alongside the tubules to receive reclaimed substances.

alternatives.reason: The collecting ducts and funnels are also needed, but I want to complete the blood connection first.

effect: The nephrons now have vessels around their recovery tubules and a venous return; the drainage route remains to be built.
reaction: The continuous vessel route makes the blood connection clearer.
reason: Join the collecting ducts to the kidney drainage funnels to build the first part of the urine outlet.
expectation: I expect a route from the collecting ducts into the renal pelvis, still needing a connection to the ureters.

alternatives.reason: The ureters and bladder also need connecting, but I will start at the kidney end.

effect: The collecting ducts now lead through calyces to a renal pelvis with an open outlet.
reaction: The picture makes the drainage sequence clear.
reason: Connect the working kidney units to their collecting route.
expectation: I expect the tubules to connect to the collecting ducts, leaving the ureter outlet to be joined later.

alternatives.reason: The ureters and bladder also need joining, but I will finish the kidney route first.

effect: The kidneys now connect filtration, recovery and collection while keeping blood and tubular fluid separate; the urine outlet still needs completing.
reaction: The parallel routes make the distinction between returned blood and urine clear.
reason: Connect the kidneys to the ureters to extend the drainage route.
expectation: I expect the renal pelvis outlets to connect to the ureters, with the bladder still to be attached.

alternatives.reason: The ureters also need to reach the bladder, but I prefer to connect them from the kidneys first.
